reasoning: In March 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated 9-dan professional Go player Lee Sedol 4 games to 1 in a five-game match in Seoul, South Korea. Prior to AlphaGo's breakthrough achievements starting with Fan Hui in late 2015 and Lee Sedol in 2016, computer science and AI experts widely believed that a computer defeating a top human Go champion was at least a decade away due to the immense game-tree complexity of Go compared to chess.
